thread:
Tomas: Quick heads-up: we're changing the default runtime quantization profile for small GPUs from 'balanced' -> 'memory-saver' to reduce OOM incidents for lightweight Dedicated tiers. This will affect a subset of customers that rely on default settings.

Asha: SDK impact: we'll add a new top-level option `quant_profile` with values: 'balanced'|'memory-saver'|'throughput'. If not provided, SDKs will follow server-side defaults (which will flip). We'll emit a single deprecation/info log for 30 days when behavior differs from a client's explicit setting.

Priya: Docs plan: migration note + quick checklist. Include example config snippets for py/js/go and a short troubleshooting section for quality regressions (how to revert to 'balanced' if needed). Draft goes to #docs-review tomorrow.

Ben: Customer Ops: we'll email affected Dedicated customers next week and give them an option to lock a runtime profile for their pool. For hosted customers we'll keep the change silent for 14 days then notify via billing dashboard and in-product banner with a link to the rollback steps.

Tomas: Rollout timeline:
- Day 0: announce + docs draft.
- Day 3: SDK patches that expose `quant_profile` param.
- Day 10: server defaults switch to 'memory-saver' on low-memory GPU classes (can be overridden).
- Day 10-30: monitoring window; revert option available on admin console.

Asha: Snippet (py):
```python
resp = client.generate("text", quant_profile="balanced")
```
If omitted, SDK will not send the header and server default applies.

Priya: I'll add a small perf-quality matrix showing token throughput vs memory for each profile.

Ben: Support checklist: how to detect quantization-induced regressions, recommended tests (perplexity on sample prompts + latency/throughput), and escalation path if customers need Dedicated pool changes.

notifier-bot: Published: Runtime quantization default update (staged docs)  https://docs.redwood.ai/quant-profiles (staging)
